Select a plan to browse its full plan_version history; drafts are edited and published here, published versions are frozen read-only.

matrix.hint: Pick a plan in the matrix above to browse its version history, or create one on an empty slot.

timeline.heading: {name} ({code}) version history
timeline.readOnly: Published versions are read-only (lock-protected); open a new draft to make changes.
timeline.pickVersion: Select a version on the left to view or edit.

editor.quotaInvalid: Quota is not valid JSON; cannot save.
editor.consumableShareHint: Credit = paid this period × [(1−α)·days-left ratio + α·consumable-quota-left ratio]; blank = default 0.5, plans without consumable quota use 0.
editor.consumableShareInvalid: α must be a number between 0 and 1.
editor.published: Published: the version is frozen and now current.

create.title: New plan · {product} · {tier}
create.description: Creates the plan skeleton (v1 draft + primary component on the tier). Prices and quota are filled on the draft; nothing is sellable before publish.
create.descPlaceholder: Optional: who this tier is for, what it includes
create.created: Plan {code} created (v1 draft) — fill prices and quota, then publish.

bundled.title: Bundled components
bundled.description: Backing products sold together with this version, each with its own quota. Infrastructure products (e.g. Atlas, Runos) have no customer plans of their own; this is the only way their quota reaches a workspace pool.
bundled.empty: No bundled component on this version yet.
bundled.quotaInvalid: Quota JSON for {name} is invalid; nothing was saved.

stats.draftsHelp: Versions still in draft and not yet frozen. Editable and deletable.
stats.sellingProductsHelp: Products with at least one published plan version. The denominator is standalone-subscribable products, not the whole catalog: bundled component products carry no tier of their own.
stats.sellingVersionsHelp: Versions pointed at by the current-version pointer, one per tier. Older versions are off sale but may still carry subscriptions.
stats.unconfiguredHelp: Products registered in the catalog with no plan at all; customers who click Subscribe land on an empty tier table.

list.empty: No standalone-subscribable products yet. Infrastructure products such as atlas and runos sell no plans of their own and only enter other versions as bundled components.
list.loadFailed: Failed to load plan publishing data.

lifecycle.currentHelp: New subscriptions pin to this version. Read-only: price and quota changes open a new version.
lifecycle.draftHelp: Not published; nobody has seen it. Editable, deletable, publishable.
lifecycle.draftOnlyVersionHelp: This is the plan's only version. Not published, nobody has seen it; deleting it deletes the whole plan and frees its plan code.
lifecycle.note: The database stores only draft and published. On sale / still serving / retired are derived from the current-version pointer and the subscription count, with no extra column.
lifecycle.retiredVersionHelp: Published but never sold a single subscription. This is the precise definition of an unused version.
lifecycle.servingHelp: No longer taking new customers, but existing ones still pay under this contract. Read-only and never deletable.

retired.description: Retiring is not deletion: the tier stops selling, but existing subscriptions still resolve against its versions, so the rows remain queryable.
retired.title: Retired

actions.deleteDraftConsequence: Draft versions have no soft-delete column; this is a hard delete of the version together with its prices and components, and cannot be undone. Published versions are unaffected.
actions.deprecateConsequence: The tier stops selling and leaves the main view, freeing the slot; existing subscriptions keep billing under their original contract. It stays visible under Retired.
actions.newPlanCodeHint: Unique and readable; used in URLs and APIs (e.g. arda-pro). Cannot be changed later.
actions.newPlanDescription: Add a plan under "{product}". Each commercial tier carries at most one live plan; occupied tiers are unavailable.
actions.newPlanDone: Plan "{name}" created; draft v1 is ready.
actions.newPlanInvalid: Plan code, plan name and tier are all required.
actions.newPlanNameHint: The name customers see on the subscription page.
actions.newVersion: Open a new draft from this version
actions.newVersionDone: A new draft was opened from v{n}.
actions.newVersionFailed: Failed to open a new draft.
actions.softDeleteConsequence: The row is deleted for good and the plan code is released for reuse. Allowed only with no live subscriptions, no order history and no solution binding: a plan that has sold can only be retired.
actions.softDeleteDone: Plan “{name}” deleted; its plan code is free again.
actions.makeInviteOnlyConsequence: This tier will no longer appear in customers' plan lists; only holders of an invitation can order it. The {n} existing subscriptions are unaffected and can still renew.
actions.makePublicConsequence: Every customer will see this tier in their plan list and can order it themselves.
actions.newVersionSameMajor: New draft from current (stay on V{v})
actions.editDescription: These are display fields ({code}). Price, quota and features are contract terms: open a new version to change them.
actions.editVisibilityHint: Being listed and being purchasable are two things: the latter is «Subscription access». An invitation tier is «not sold publicly, but visible to invitation holders».

detail.blockedHint: Not cleanable: subscriptions, subscription history or orders still reference it.
detail.crowdedHint: More than one plan sits on this tier. The database allows it, but customers only ever see the one currently on sale.
detail.tierDescription: Which tiers this product sells, which version each is on, and who subscribes. A tier may carry more than one plan — the database allows it, and cards flag the ones that do.

editorV2.actionsLeftHint: Left side is reversible: save and discard can both be redone.
editorV2.actionsRightHint: Right side is not: publishing freezes this version, after which only a new draft can change anything.
editorV2.alphaHint: α is a pricing parameter, not a quota, so it sits beside price and ahead of quota. It used to hide inside the quota JSON, making people edit two different things in one box while it directly drives revenue.
editorV2.alphaInvalid: α must be a number between 0 and 1.
editorV2.amountInvalid: The amount for {key} must be a number (-1 means unlimited, meaningful only for max-type keys).
editorV2.bundleChosenEmpty: This tier wires in no other product's backend capability.
editorV2.bundleHint: Which products' backend capability is wired in. What comes in has no front end and is invisible to the user; the product's own UI and full features need their own subscription.
editorV2.bundleNoCandidates: No bindable products. Only L2 domain-platform products can contribute backend capability.
editorV2.byteHint: Converted at 1024 per step; the stored value is always raw bytes — that is what the preview shows.
editorV2.chosenEmpty: No quota item chosen yet. Add one from the left.
editorV2.groupProductHint: Registered by this product, pooled only here
editorV2.notDraft: This version is not a draft and cannot be edited. Published versions are lock-protected; open a new draft to change them.
editorV2.previewHint: What actually goes into plan_components.quota, recomputed live from the choices above. No need to open it normally — it exists for one case: when you suspect the picker assembled something wrong and want to check on the spot.
editorV2.priorityHint: Order is burn order, not layout: every bundled component's priority must be lower than the primary's (primary 100, bundled 50 by default), meaning bundled allowance burns before the product's own pool. Getting it wrong bills the customer in the wrong order.
editorV2.published: Published and set as the live version.
editorV2.quotaHint: Candidates on the left, what this tier actually grants on the right. Pick, reorder, remove — no JSON.
editorV2.subtitle: {tier} tier draft · frozen once published
editorV2.title: {plan} · v{n}

readonly.draftOpenFailed: Failed to open a new draft.
readonly.locked: A published version cannot change: triggers forbid inserting, updating or deleting even its child rows. Open a new version instead.
readonly.openNextDraft: Open a new draft from this
readonly.openNextDraftHint: It does not change this version; it clones the content into a new one — published versions are immutable, so changing means a new version.

rejectDeclaration.title: Reject payment declaration
rejectDeclaration.description: Order {orderNo}. Vouchers and discounts are released, the order goes back to awaiting payment, and the reason is shown on the customer's payment page.
rejectDeclaration.reasonHint: Required, at least 4 characters; the customer will see it.
rejectDeclaration.placeholder: e.g. No matching transfer found, please check the amount and pay again; received 500 but 860 was declared.
rejectDeclaration.descriptionWithAmount: Order {orderNo} · customer declared {amount}. Vouchers and discounts are released, the order goes back to awaiting payment, and the reason is shown on the customer's payment page.

refund.titleComplete: Refund completed (paid out through the original channel)
refund.descApprove: Refund {refundNo} · {amount}. After approving, pay out through the original channel, then come back and click "Refund completed".
refund.descReject: Refund {refundNo} · {amount}. The reason is shown to the customer.
refund.descComplete: Refund {refundNo} · {amount}. On execution the order becomes refunded, the product subscription goes back to unsubscribed as a whole (including the free tier before an upgrade), entitlements stop immediately, and any credit overflow that went to prepaid balance is reversed.
refund.remarkHintCustomer: Required, at least 4 characters; the customer will see it.
refund.placeholderComplete: e.g. Returned ¥0.10 via Alipay on 9/4, transaction no. …
refund.placeholderReview: e.g. Qualifies for the 24-hour first-purchase refund; or: outside the refund window / usage over threshold.
refund.descApproveWithReason: Refund {refundNo} · {amount} · customer's reason: {reason}. After approving, pay out through the original channel, then come back and click "Refund completed".
refund.descRejectWithReason: Refund {refundNo} · {amount} · customer's reason: {reason}. The reason is shown to the customer.
refund.descCompleteWithReason: Refund {refundNo} · {amount} · customer's reason: {reason}. On execution the order becomes refunded, the product subscription goes back to unsubscribed as a whole (including the free tier before an upgrade), entitlements stop immediately, and any credit overflow that went to prepaid balance is reversed.
refund.titleFail: Payout failed (money did not go out)
refund.descFail: Refund {refundNo} · {amount}. Marking it failed leaves the order and subscription unchanged (no money went out, service continues as is); the customer receives a "could not complete" notice. They can request again, but the 24-hour refund window keeps running.
refund.descFailWithReason: Refund {refundNo} · {amount} · customer's reason: {reason}. Marking it failed leaves the order and subscription unchanged (no money went out, service continues as is); the customer receives a "could not complete" notice. They can request again, but the 24-hour refund window keeps running.
refund.placeholderFail: e.g. Transfer bounced by the bank on 9/25, account number and holder name do not match
refund.descCreate: This order was paid {amount}. This path skips the three policy checks (time window, first purchase, usage ratio); unprovisioned, ¥0 and orders with a refund already in flight are still refused (that is fact and ledger integrity, not policy). The amount is prorated by consumed quota; it still needs review and then execution.
refund.placeholderCreate: e.g. 6-hour outage on 9/20, compensation agreed with the customer (ticket 123)

restoreOrder.title: Restore order
restoreOrder.description: Order {orderNo}. The order goes back to awaiting payment; the bill and discounts are restored with it.
restoreOrder.reasonHint: Required, at least 4 characters; recorded in the order timeline.
restoreOrder.placeholder: e.g. Customer confirmed they still want to buy; voided by mistake, restoring.
restoreOrder.descriptionWithTenant: Order {orderNo} · {tenantName}. The order goes back to awaiting payment; the bill and discounts are restored with it.

voidOrder.title: Void order
voidOrder.description: Order {orderNo}. After voiding, the order no longer waits for payment; the customer must place a new order to buy.
voidOrder.descriptionWithTenant: Order {orderNo} · {tenantName}. After voiding, the order no longer waits for payment; the customer must place a new order to buy.
voidOrder.reasonHint: Required, at least 4 characters; recorded in the order timeline.
voidOrder.placeholder: e.g. Customer cancelled by phone, duplicate order.

orderHint.paid_unprovisioned: Money received; the system is provisioning
orderHint.partial_pending: Legacy order: part of the money arrived; waiting for the rest or an offline arrangement
orderHint.closed: Cancelled by the customer or timed out unpaid

orderHint.overdue: The payment deadline passed; waiting for the system to close it
orderHint.abnormal: Unexpected state; ask technical support to check

title.pending: Wait for the customer to pay and declare
title.partial_pending: Partially received, waiting for the rest

body.pending: After paying, the customer declares it on the payment page. Nothing for you to do yet. If they do not pay in time the system closes the order.
body.pending_verify: If the money arrived, click "Confirm payment". If you cannot find it or the amount differs, click "Reject declaration" and say why; the customer is notified and can declare again.
body.paid_unprovisioned: The system provisions automatically, usually within two minutes. If it is still here after ten minutes, click "Provision again".
body.partial_pending: Legacy order: {received} has arrived, {remaining} is still missing. Confirm the rest once the customer pays it, or settle it offline.
body.confirmed: This order is done. If the customer asks, the validity and auto-renew setting are under "After provisioning" below.
body.closed: Reason: {reason}. If the customer still wants to buy, you can restore the order (only orders that never received money can be restored).
body.refunded: The money went back to the customer and the subscription is back to unsubscribed.
body.refundPending: The customer requested a refund of {amount}. If it qualifies, approve it, pay out through the original channel, then come back and click "Refund completed"; otherwise reject it and say why.
body.refundApproved: The refund of {amount} is approved. After paying out click "Refund completed"; if the money did not go out click "Payout failed".
body.refundFailed: The last payout of {amount} did not go through. Check the receiving account and pay again; click "Refund completed" on success, or record "Payout failed" again.
body.abnormal: The state is unexpected and cannot be acted on here. Send the order number to technical support.

timeline.title: Handling timeline
timeline.description: Every entry says whether the customer can see it.
timeline.emptyDescription: No replies, notes, assignments or status changes on this ticket yet.

reply.title: Reply to the customer
reply.description: This is written for the customer: they read it in full on their own ticket. Once sent it cannot be edited or taken back.
reply.label: Your reply
reply.placeholder: Written for the customer to read…

note.title: Internal note
note.description: Operations only: the customer never sees internal notes on this ticket and is never sent them.
note.label: Your note
note.placeholder: What was agreed, your own read on it, what the next shift needs to know…
note.success: Saved as an internal note — the customer cannot see it

close.title: Close ticket
close.consequence: Closing says this piece of support is over. The customer sees the close on their own ticket, and once they do they stop waiting on your reply. Picking it up again means reopening this ticket or logging a new one.
close.reasonHint: The customer reads this line: it shows up on their own ticket as the reason you closed it. Keep internal reasons out of here — put those in an internal note.
close.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Handled as agreed with you; if it happens again, just reply on this ticket…
close.alreadyFinal: This ticket is already final — closed, or cancelled — so there is nothing to close. Reload the page to see where it stands.

statusDialog.title: Change ticket status
statusDialog.noteHint: The customer reads this line: it shows up on their own ticket as the progress note for this step. Keep your own read on it out of here — put that in an internal note.
statusDialog.notePlaceholder: e.g. We found the cause and are on it; we will reply on this ticket once it is fixed…
statusDialog.closeHint: Closed is not on this list. Use Close ticket at the top of the page — that dialog first spells out what closing means for the customer.
statusDialog.failed: Could not change the status. Try again.

create.title: New ticket
create.description: Log a ticket for a customer — something they reported by phone, email or chat.
create.tenantHint: Search by tenant number or name. The ticket belongs to the whole tenant, so every member there can see it — not just the person who reported it.
create.tenantsFailed: Could not load the tenant list
create.tenantsFailedDetail: Without the tenant list there is no customer to pick, so this ticket cannot be created yet. Reload the page; if it keeps failing, call the platform on-call.
create.titleHint: One line on what the customer ran into. They see this title on their own ticket.
create.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Report export stuck on generating
create.priorityHint: P0 means the customer is already blocked and someone has to pick it up now. When in doubt leave it at P2.
create.reporterHint: Who raised it. Leaving it empty is fine — the ticket belongs to the whole tenant, so it does not have to name a person.
create.reporterPlaceholder: e.g. their ops engineer (empty means no one named)
create.descriptionHint: Write it in the customer's own words. They read this on their own ticket, so keep your own read on it out of here — add that as an internal note once the ticket exists.
create.descriptionPlaceholder: What they said, what they already tried, what they expected…

digest.descriptionUnread: Platform notices from opera and the product side: launches, new capabilities, change notices. {unread} unread.

states.emptyDigestDescription: Unread messages and the ones you read today are listed here; older ones live under All messages.
states.emptyAllDescription: Notices published from opera, and the operator mirror of customer payments, refunds and cancellations, will show up here.

actionDialog.reasonHint: The customer reads this wording exactly as you write it. Write one sentence they can understand, with no internal shorthand or codes.

disable.title: Disable account
disable.description: Disables {name} ({email}): every sign-in path is blocked and all sessions are revoked. It can be restored later. The reason you write is passed on to that customer.
disable.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Unusual sign-in activity was found on this account, so it is disabled for now; contact support to verify your identity and have it restored.

enable.title: Restore account
enable.description: Returns the account of {name} to normal. The reason you write is passed on to that customer.
enable.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Identity verification passed, the account is back to normal use.

forceLogout.title: Sign out everywhere
forceLogout.description: Revokes every active session of {name}; they will have to sign in again. The reason you write is passed on to that customer.
forceLogout.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. An unfamiliar device was signed in, so all sessions were ended; change your password and sign in again.
